chunks: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“If a man forgets to wash his right hand, then he washes his left hand and wipes his head and his feet, then remembers after that, he should wash his right hand and his left hand, then wipe his head and his feet. But if he only forgot his left hand, then let him wash the left hand, and he does not repeat what he had performed of wudu (ablution).”
He said: “And perform the parts of your wudu (ablution) one after another.”

key_terms.بَعْضَهُ بَعْضًا: one part after another, indicating continuity and ordered succession
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, over which wiping is performed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, which are wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.شِمَالَهُ: his left hand, whose omission has a distinct legal ruling here
key_terms.وُضُوءَكَ: your wudu (ablution), referring to the ritual act of purification
key_terms.يَمِينَهُ: his right hand, whose omission affects the sequence of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets to wash one hand during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who forgets part of wudu (ablution), distinguishing between forgetting the right hand and forgetting the left hand. It also emphasizes maintaining the proper sequence and continuity in wudu (ablution), making it an important text in the fiqh of ritual purity.
